nodes.name: Webhook — New Application
nodes.notes: Entry point. Receives application payload from mock ATS or real ATS (Greenhouse, Workday). Shape: { application_id, candidate_id, job_posting_id } — these are written to Supabase by /api/webhooks/application-received before n8n is called.

nodes.name: HTTP — Extract Resume Text
nodes.notes: Calls Next.js backend to download resume from Supabase Storage and extract plain text. Result stored in applications.resume_text.

nodes.name: HTTP — Score Resume (LLM Call 1)
nodes.notes: Calls Next.js backend which assembles job rubric + resume text, calls gpt-4o-mini for structured per-criterion scoring, stores result in resume_scores, sets status=pending_review.

nodes.name: HTTP — Store n8n Resume URL
nodes.notes: CRITICAL STEP: Saves the Wait node's unique resume URL to the database. Without this, the paused workflow can NEVER be resumed when a recruiter makes a decision days later. This is the most commonly missed step in this pattern.

nodes.name: Wait — Human Decision Required
nodes.notes: Workflow GENUINELY PAUSES here. Not polling — the execution is frozen until /api/applications/[id]/decision calls this node's resumeUrl. This is what makes the human-in-the-loop pattern real.

nodes.name: IF — Approved?
nodes.notes: Branches on the decision value sent in the resume URL call. Never branches on LLM output.

nodes.name: IF — Rejected?
nodes.notes: Second branch check for rejection. If neither approved nor rejected, falls through to more_info.

nodes.name: HTTP — Create Interview Slots
nodes.notes: Creates 2-3 interview slot rows in the database. Candidate will pick from these.

parameters.subject: Interview Invitation — {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.job_title }}
parameters.message:
Hi {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.candidate_name }},

Congratulations! We'd like to invite you to interview for the {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.job_title }} position.

Please select your preferred interview time: {{ $env.APP_BASE_URL }}/interviews/{{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.application_id }}/confirm

Best regards,
The Hiring Team

nodes.name: Email — Interview Invitation
nodes.notes: Sends interview invitation email with link to /interviews/[id]/confirm — the candidate-facing slot picker page.

parameters.subject: Your application for {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.job_title }}
parameters.message:
Hi {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.candidate_name }},

Thank you for your interest in the {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.job_title }} position.

After careful review, we've decided to move forward with other candidates whose experience more closely matches our current needs.

We appreciate the time you invested in applying and wish you the best in your search.

Best regards,
The Hiring Team

nodes.name: Email — Rejection
nodes.notes: Rejection email. Only sent after explicit human decision — never triggered by LLM output.

parameters.subject: Additional information needed — {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.job_title }}
parameters.message:
Hi {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.candidate_name }},

Thank you for applying to the {{ $('Webhook — New Application').item.json.job_title }} position.

We'd like to learn more before moving forward. A member of our team will be in touch shortly with specific questions.

Best regards,
The Hiring Team

nodes.name: Email — More Info Request
nodes.notes: Sent when recruiter requests more information. Workflow can loop back to Wait after response.

nodes.name: Respond to Webhook
nodes.notes: Sends immediate 200 response to the ATS webhook trigger so it doesn't time out waiting.

meta.description: HireFlow recruitment pipeline — webhook trigger → resume extract → LLM score → Wait (human review) → branch on decision → email. The Wait node genuinely pauses until the recruiter approves/rejects via the dashboard.
